transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood SE), Ava (NovaHealth), Connor (NovaHealth), Maya (NovaHealth Security), Ethan (NovaHealth SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check-in today, we'll run through the benchmark slides and the comparison vs what the customer ran with ProviderX, and then call out next steps, ok?
[00:12] Ava: Yep that's the plan, excited to see the numbers. We've been running the baseline on their managed endpoint for the last two weeks.
[00:18] Lena: Cool. I'm going to share my screen, got the benchmark summary csv open, there might be some typos in the labels, transcription sometimes flips model names.
[00:28] Jules: Quick note, for context we used the same prompt set you provided last week, 60/40 split short/long and a 128/512/1k token distribution for the run.
[00:38] Connor: Confirmed. Baseline was ProviderX standard instance type - they used their default batching and no quantization.
[00:44] [00:45] Lena: OK first slide median latency 512 tokens, baseline ProviderX median 242ms, Redwood POC median 195ms, that's about 19% lower median latency for us. Now p95 baseline 480ms vs Redwood 410ms. Throughput numbers, tail-throughput for concurrent 20 clients, baseline ~110 rps, Redwood ~145 rps so about 1.32x.
[01:10] Ava: That's promising. Can you remind us what config you were running on Redwood side?
[01:14] Lena: Sure, this run used a dedicated test pool - 2x A100-like cards per node, inference engine with 4-bit quantization profile q4_0 for the encoder, KV cache enabled, continuous batching window tuned to 8ms and max batch size 64, also prefix caching for repeated prompts. The baseline didn't use quantization or prefix caching.
[01:34] Ethan: Were both runs warm start? Sometimes ProviderX numbers drop after cache warm up.
[01:38] Lena: Yes both had warm-up period, we did 5k warmup requests. The difference persists after warmup. Also we noticed Redwood's KV cache cut per-token compute on repeat prompts by ~30%.
[01:50] Connor: What about quality delta with q4? Any hallucination increase or response degradation?
[01:54] Lena: We ran the quality check with your scoring harness; delta was within noise for majority of prompts, about a 0.6% increase in generation time-to-first-token but no statistically significant Rouge/BLEU changes. We did see a handful of edge cases on long doc summarization where q4 needed fallback to q8, we captured those in the logs.
[02:14] Ava: Good to call out. For compliance, Maya, any blocker on quantization?
[02:18] Maya: Not on quantization per se, more concerned about encryption in transit and key management. We need KMS integration and customer-managed keys. Also SSO roles mapping, and audit logs retention.
[02:28] Samir: That's expected. Redwood Private supports bring-your-own-KMS and we've got audit logs that can be shipped to your SIEM. I'll share the docs.
[02:35] Maya: Please include retention options and whether logs include token-level metadata or only request/response ids.
[02:40] Samir: We'll clarify - our default includes request and response ids and sizes; token-level payloads require specific agreement, we'll note that.
[02:48] [03:00] Jules: Back to perf - we also ran a mixed workload with longer context 1k tokens, baseline median 410ms vs Redwood 340ms, throughput 74 rps vs 96 rps. We included a run with CPU fallback and that's where the delta narrows.
[03:20] Connor: Any tuning knobs left we haven't tried? E.g., lower batch window or custom kernel selection?
[03:26] Lena: Yes we can tune the batching window down to 4ms but that trades throughput; kernel selection is auto in our runtime, but we can force a variant for a single run. We also want to test larger max batch sizes for high concurrency.
[03:38] Ava: Can you also run a 4k token end-to-end test? That's our main concern for long context meds triage.
[03:43] Lena: Yep we can. That will take a few hours to run and generate big logs - I'll schedule overnight and share results.
[03:49] [04:00] Samir: Pricing question - if we move to dedicated, what's the expected committed throughput needed and pricing tiers?
[04:05] Samir (cont): I'll send the updated pricing sheet. For a mid-tier commit we can guarantee 95th perc latency SLAs and provide reserved capacity with burst.
[04:12] Ava: Great. Any notes on network egress and region placement? We need EU residency for some customers.
[04:18] Jules: Redwood Dedicated can pin region; Private deployment options for on-prem/VPC are possible for regulated datasets. For EU residency we'll deploy in eu-west-1 region nodes.
[04:26] Maya: Audit question again - can Redwood provide SOC2 report and iso docs?
[04:30] Samir: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs - we'll share the security pack. Also SAML SSO is supported with SCIM and RBAC mapping.
[04:39] Ethan: One more curiosity - how deterministic are your latency numbers day-to-day? We saw ProviderX variance across times.
[04:45] Lena: We measured across 48 hours, Redwood variance was lower: stdev 12% vs baseline 22% on the same workload. The variance goes up during nightly batch jobs but routing policies avoid co-tenancy.
[04:57] Ava: Any mention of cold-starts? ProviderX had big cold starts for large models.
[05:02] Jules: Redwood's runtime keeps KV caches warm and supports hot-pools to avoid cold penalty; cold starts still happen on scaled-to-zero but not in Dedicated.
[05:13] [05:15] Connor: Are there any known incompatibilities with our infra? We run on our VPC peering and use private subnets.
[05:20] Samir: For Private we can install the control plane in your VPC with private endpoints; peering and firewall rules are standard. We'll provide the network diagram.
[05:27] Maya: Please include HSM/KMS architecture options.
[05:30] Samir: Will do.
[05:32] [06:00] Lena: Quick note on the anomaly we saw: a couple of requests spiked to p99 1.9s, looks correlated with long-token outliers and fallback to q8. We'll include those traces.
[06:12] Ava: Ok that's helpful.
[06:15] Samir: Recap - Lena will run 4k token tests and share logs by Tues, I'll send pricing and security pack by Fri, customer to confirm compliance stakeholders. Let's schedule the exec review for the 19th.
[06:30] Ava: Sounds good thanks everyone.
[06:33] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up in email.

Meeting End
questions: What is the expected latency improvement for 4k token workloads?
Can Redwood support BYOK KMS and what logs are retained?
What's the committed capacity pricing tiers for Dedicated?
